summary.en: XIAO is Seeed Studio’s most popular thumb-sized, powerful microcontroller units (MCUs), tailor-made for space-conscious projects that requir
summary.zh: XIAO is Seeed Studio’s most popular thumb-sized, powerful microcontroller units (MCUs), tailor-made for space-conscious projects that requir

proposed.en: XIAO is Seeed Studio’s most popular thumb-sized, powerful microcontroller units (MCUs), tailor-made for space-conscious projects that require high performance and wireless connectivity. Over the years, the XIAO family has expanded to include eight core boards, featuring mainstream hardware platforms such as ESP32, RP2040, nRF52840, and SAMD21. As user applications become increasingly diverse, users need more than just XIAO’s mini size; they also require more chip I/O interface expansion capabilities. Currently, the 14 pins seem somewhat insufficient. Therefore, we are now looking for a clever way to expand the number of I/Os to meet the more complex and varied user product design needs. Today, we're proposing an expansion method and hope that the enthusiastic community will provide valuabl

title.en: Connect XIAO to Cloud (SenseCraft Data platform)
title.zh: Connect XIAO to Cloud (SenseCraft Data platform)

summary.en: Many XIAO users have turned their devices into IoT or AI devices, but the data produced by these devices or the results of AI inference requ
summary.zh: Many XIAO users have turned their devices into IoT or AI devices, but the data produced by these devices or the results of AI inference requ

proposed.en: Many XIAO users have turned their devices into IoT or AI devices, but the data produced by these devices or the results of AI inference require secondary integration development to be fully analyzed and viewed. In fact, Seeed already has a software platform previously used for Industrial IoT devices, such as LoRaWAN sensors and 4G collectors, which allows for easy device data viewing and management by simply scanning a QR code and binding the device. XIAO users, do you need a simple and easy-to-use cloud platform that can directly support XIAO data? Please leave your comments or suggest some feature requirements.

proposed.en: Currently, all XIAO Boards except the newest member XIAO ESP32C6 are compatible with the Linux Zephyr project thanks to the support and contribution from the community! Now, we're calling for your support to add Zephyr support for this new board, please start with the Zephyr Board Porting Guide. summary.zh: image I had trouble fitting the Xiao into my 3D printed projects because it doesn't have any screw holes. While glue is an option for some p

proposed.en: image I had trouble fitting the Xiao into my 3D printed projects because it doesn't have any screw holes. While glue is an option for some projects, it's not ideal if we need to regularly connect and disconnect the USB. Some makers don't require a custom PCB for simple projects, so the only option for them to securely fit the Xiao in the project is to glue it. Additionally, if we need to connect the battery in the Xiao ESP32C3, we have to solder wires on the back side of the Xiao, which prevents it from laying flat on a 3D printed surface. just in order to solve this problem I come up with this idea , I small PCB adapter . summary.en: XIAO has never had a dedicated LoRa extension board. Now, we have developed a LoRa module based on the Semtech SX1262 chip, and used this mo
summary.zh: XIAO has never had a dedicated LoRa extension board. Now, we have developed a LoRa module based on the Semtech SX1262 chip, and used this mo

proposed.en: XIAO has never had a dedicated LoRa extension board. Now, we have developed a LoRa module based on the Semtech SX1262 chip, and used this module to create an extension board for XIAO. This board communicates with XIAO via SPI, allowing XIAO nRF52840 or XIAO ESP32 to develop applications based on LoRa or LoRaWAN. Please share your thoughts with us, so we can quickly design a module or extension board that meets everyone's needs. Wio-SX1262 DSC01075

proposed.en: A programmer-debugger probe is a very useful and "must have" tool for embedded system development. Today, there is no affordable offer. Segger used to list the J-Link Edu mini probe at an affordable price; it is no longer the case. Price went from USD20 to USD70. The Xiao expansion board provides the pogo pins to make the connections, alas only for some boards, SAMD, nRF52840 and RP2040. Once the Xiao is mounted in the final design, the SWD pads are no longer accessible unless they are rerouted. summary.en: Hi everyone, I’m Ellie, Product Marketing Manager at Seeed Studio, covering the XIAO product line. Recently, Espressif introduced the new ES
summary.zh: Hi everyone, I’m Ellie, Product Marketing Manager at Seeed Studio, covering the XIAO product line. Recently, Espressif introduced the new ES

proposed.en: Hi everyone, I’m Ellie, Product Marketing Manager at Seeed Studio, covering the XIAO product line. Recently, Espressif introduced the new ESP32-S31 SoC — a high-performance dual-core 32-bit RISC-V MCU running at up to 320 MHz. We’ve been taking a close look at the specs and evaluating how this new chip could fit into the XIAO ecosystem, and we’d love to hear the community’s perspective as well. Are the ESP32-S31’s power-efficiency improvements compelling enough to justify a new XIAO variant, or do you feel the current ESP32-S3 lineup already hits the right balance of performance, features, and power consumption? My colleague Josie also published a detailed comparison between the ESP32-S31 and ESP32-S3 here: https://www.seeedstudio.com/blog/2026/04/14/esp32-s31-vs-esp32-s3-should-the-xiao-g

proposed.en: Hello everyone, We are currently experimenting a new XIAO add-on and we want to hear your thoughts! Many developers told us they wanted an easier way to access every XIAO pin during prototyping, debugging, sensor testing, etc. This GPIO breakout board for XIAO is our attempt to make the 1.27mm-pitch IOs and BAT pins easier to access and solder, especially for prototyping. Would you use something like this, and what would you like to add? Please feel free to leave comments as it will be useful inputs for future revisions. (P.S. The XIAO shown in the image was soldered on for demonstration purposes and is not included with the board.)
